Q: How to solve mobile virtual keyboard overlaps TextMesh Input-fields? And also Virtual keyboard reopens when switch between input-fields A:

To answer your second question first, you can check the TouchScreenKeyboard.area property, which will tell you the screen area occupied by the touch keyboard. Then you can modify the position of the controls specifically to avoid overlapping.

Alternatively, you can uncheck "Hide Mobile Input" on the input field control to display a native input field above the keyboard.

As for your first question, different input fields often require the use of different keyboard types (number, password, etc.), so switching keyboards is inevitable.

Secondly, whether it is InputField or TMP_InputField, the keyboard will automatically hide when the focus is lost. If you want to maintain the display status, you can create your own inheritance type to replace the default keyboard process (for TMP_InputField, you can set shouldHideSoftKeyboard = false). Or use the TouchScreenKeyboard class to implement your own input field. (You can find the source code of the InputField class in Unity's installation directory)

Q: Result order of string_split? A:

Original answer:

Starting from SQL Server 2016, you may use a JSON-based approach. You simply need to transform the input string into a valid JSON array (b,a,c is transformed into ["b","a","c"]) and then parse this array with OPENJSON() and default schema. The result is a table with columns key, value and type, and based on the documentation, the key column is an nvarchar(4000) value that contains the name of the specified property or the index of the element in the specified array.

DECLARE @StringToSplit VARCHAR(100) = 'b,a,c';

SELECT [value]
FROM OPENJSON(CONCAT('["', REPLACE(@StringToSplit, ',', '","'), '"]'))
ORDER BY CONVERT(int, [key])
value
b
a
c

Note, that starting from SQL Server 2017, you have an option to remove possible quotes in the input JSON using the STRING_ESCAPE() function:

DECLARE @StringToSplit VARCHAR(100) = '"b",''a'',c';

SELECT [value]
FROM OPENJSON(CONCAT('["', REPLACE(STRING_ESCAPE(@StringToSplit, 'json'), ',', '","'), '"]'))
ORDER BY CONVERT(int, [key])

Result:

value
"b"
'a'
c

Update:

Starting from SQL Server 2022, the STRING_SPLIT() function supports an optional third parameter enable_ordinal. The parameter is an int or bit expression that serves as a flag to enable or disable the ordinal output column. A value of 1 enables the ordinal column. If enable_ordinal is omitted, NULL, or has a value of 0, the ordinal column is disabled.

SELECT [value]
FROM STRING_SPLIT(@StringToSplit, ',', 1)
ORDER BY [ordinal]

Q: Implicit AsQueryable A:

How do the base providers accomplish this implicit use of AsQueryable?

They don't. Your code doesn't really execute FirstOrDefault() at all. It builds an expression tree which represents the call, but that isn't executed directly. The query provider sees that, works out that the f.PersonHistories is actually based on an entity which is in the database, and converts the query appropriately.
